beats.text: For years, couples raced to one Indiana town to get married with no waiting. Crown Point became known as the marriage mill.
beats.label: CROWN POINT, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: Indiana State Library; Crown Point Community Library

beats.text: Indiana had no waiting period for a marriage license. So couples from Chicago crossed the state line.
beats.label: ACROSS THE STATE LINE
beats.credit: Indiana State Library; Crown Point Community Library

beats.text: On March 14, 1923, the silent film star Rudolph Valentino married Natacha Rambova in Crown Point.
beats.label: MARCH 14, 1923: ACROSS FROM THE COURTHOUSE
beats.credit: Time magazine, 1923; WBEZ; Indiana State Library

beats.text: The rush faded around 1940, after Indiana tightened its marriage laws, including a required blood test.
beats.label: THE LAW CHANGED
beats.credit: Indiana State Library; Crown Point Community Library

beats.text: The courthouse went up starting in 1878. They call it the Grand Old Lady. It was once threatened with demolition for a parking lot, until residents saved it.
beats.label: THE GRAND OLD LADY
beats.credit: Advisory Council on Historic Preservation; Lake Court House Foundation

beats.text: Today it holds shops. And couples still get married there.
beats.label: TODAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
